gap: No result ChatGPT got says which battery inverter can run which SubDrive Connect. Franklin's own generator rule (1.5 × the drive's maximum input watts, minimums 3,500 / 5,700 / 7,000 / 11,000 W for SubDrive 15/20/30/50) sets the bar. A single 6,000 W split-phase inverter clears it for the SubDrive20 by only 1.05× and falls short of the SubDrive30 at 0.86×.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited. The SubDrive/MonoDrive FAQ gives only the 190–260 VAC input range and says soft start means 'lower start-up current'. The SubDrive Connect product page gives only '1/2 – 5 hp' and 'soft start', with no input watts and no generator or inverter sizing. The uncited SubDrive Connect manual in ChatGPT's results (franklinagua PDF, manualslib copy) has the generator-minimum table on page 12. That is part of the input, but no result connects it to an inverter's continuous rating, and none mentions an inverter at all. ChatGPT's own answer stops at 'pure sine wave inverter with high surge capacity', which is the wrong number to size on when a SubDrive soft-starts the motor.
decides: It changes how the page should frame the pick. For a SubDrive (the pick ChatGPT made), continuous watts at 240 V decide the inverter, not surge. Under Franklin's rule, the SPH6548P (6,500 W, 1.14× the SubDrive20 minimum, $1,035) is the cheapest listed unit that clears a SubDrive20 from one box. The Sun Gold 6000W LF and the EG4 6000XP clear it by only 5% (1.05×). No single listed unit covers a SubDrive30 (needs 7,000 W). One Victron MultiPlus-II 120V can't feed a SubDrive at all, since the drive needs 190–260 VAC, so a pair (8,000 W) is the minimum. For a plain across-the-line pump with no drive, surge would still decide, but I couldn't source the locked-rotor amps for that comparison.
candidates: Sun Gold Power SPH6548P 6.5 kW hybrid

findings.label: Franklin SubDrive Connect generator sizing rule
findings.value: 1.5 × the drive's maximum input watts, rounded up to the next normal generator size
findings.source_title: Franklin Electric SubDrive Connect Owner's Manual, p. 12 'Generator Sizing' (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Quoted from the manual. Franklin writes this rule for generators. Using it for an inverter's continuous rating is our proxy.

findings.label: Recommended minimum generator watts by SubDrive Connect model
findings.value: SubDrive15 3,500 W; SubDrive20 5,700 W; SubDrive30 7,000 W; SubDrive50 11,000 W
findings.source_title: Franklin Electric SubDrive Connect Owner's Manual, p. 12 (ManualsLib)
findings.note: The extracted text listed models and watts in the same order but not side by side, so this pairing follows table order.

findings.label: Implied maximum drive input power (upper bound)
findings.value: SubDrive15 ≤2,333 W; SubDrive20 ≤3,800 W; SubDrive30 ≤4,667 W; SubDrive50 ≤7,333 W
findings.source_title: Franklin Electric SubDrive Connect Owner's Manual, p. 12 (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Generator minimum ÷ 1.5: 3,500/1.5=2,333; 5,700/1.5=3,800; 7,000/1.5=4,667; 11,000/1.5=7,333. These are upper bounds because Franklin rounds up to a standard generator size.

findings.label: SubDrive/MonoDrive input voltage and soft start
findings.value: Line voltage 190–260 VAC (F2 undervoltage fault below 180 VAC, measured L1–L2); soft start gives 'lower start-up current' (2-wire motors have no soft start)
findings.note: Because the drive needs 240 V, any 120 V-only inverter (one MultiPlus-II 120V) is ruled out unless two are stacked for split phase. Because of soft start, continuous watts matter more than surge.
